questions.question: Where was the 2025 Wimbledon tennis tournament held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London, United Kingdom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Wimbledon tennis tournament** is held annually in **London, United Kingdom**, at the **All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club**.
 
• This tournament is one of the **four Grand Slam events** in tennis, the other three being the Australian Open, French Open, and US Open.
 
• Wimbledon is renowned for being the **oldest tennis tournament in the world**, first held in the year **1877**.
 
• The event is unique as it is the only Grand Slam played on **grass courts**, maintaining its traditional setting and historical significance.
 
• It takes place over two weeks in late **June and early July** and is famous for its traditions, such as a strict dress code for players, royal patronage, and serving **strawberries and cream** to spectators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Wimbledon:**

 
 
• The tournament is hosted by the **All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club**, located in the Wimbledon district of London.
 
• It is considered the most prestigious tennis event due to its rich **history** and adherence to tradition.
 
• The event features five main competitions: **Men’s Singles, Women’s Singles, Men’s Doubles, Women’s Doubles, and Mixed Doubles**, along with junior and invitational matches.
 
 
 
• **Other Grand Slam Tournaments:**
 
 
• **Australian Open:** Held in **Melbourne, Australia**, it is played on **hard courts** and marks the first Grand Slam of the calendar year.
 
• **French Open:** Known as **Roland Garros**, it is held in **Paris, France**, and is played on **clay courts**.
 
• **US Open:** Hosted in **New York, USA**, it is also played on **hard courts** and is the final Grand Slam of the year.
 
 
 
• **Notable Wimbledon Traditions:**
 
 
• Players must adhere to a strict **all-white dress code** while competing on the court.
 
• The tournament is attended by members of the **British Royal Family**, adding a prestigious aura to the event.
 
• It is famous for its **strawberries and cream**, with approximately 28,000 kilograms of strawberries consumed during the tournament.
 
 
 
• **Historical Importance:**
 
 
• First played in **1877**, Wimbledon is the oldest tennis tournament in the world and has been held annually except during the **World Wars** and the **COVID-19 pandemic in 2020**.
 
• It has seen legendary players like **Roger Federer, Serena Williams, Novak Djokovic, and Martina Navratilova** achieve historic victories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prize Money:** Wimbledon offers significant prize money, which has steadily increased over the years to reward players for their performances.
 
• **Technology:** Wimbledon employs advanced technologies like **Hawk-Eye** to assist in line calls and ensure fair gameplay.
 
• **Centre Court Roof:** The main court at Wimbledon, Centre Court, has a retractable roof to allow play to continue in adverse weather conditions.
 
• **Wildcard Entries:** The tournament often grants wildcard entries to deserving players based on their past achievements or potential.

questions.question: What scientific activity is NOT planned on Axiom‑4?

options.text: Testing crewed docking with a lunar base at Indian space station
Studying the effects of short spaceflights on joints and blood flow
Examining microgravity's impact on the brain and cognitive risks
Understanding the effects on blood stem cells during spaceflight

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Testing crewed docking with a lunar base at Indian space station**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Testing crewed docking with a lunar base** at an **Indian space station** is not a planned scientific activity under the Axiom‑4 mission. The mission primarily focuses on microgravity experiments and health-related studies, not lunar exploration or docking tests.
 
• The Axiom‑4 mission is part of **Axiom Space's commercial spaceflight program**, aimed at conducting research aboard the **International Space Station (ISS)**. The mission does not involve testing docking capabilities for lunar bases or collaboration with Indian space stations.
 
• Statement 2, which mentions **studying the effects of short spaceflights on joints and blood flow**, is correct. This aligns with the mission’s objective to understand how microgravity impacts human health during short-duration spaceflights.
 
• Statement 3 is accurate as the mission plans to investigate **microgravity's impact on the brain** and assess potential cognitive risks to astronauts, a critical area of study for long-term space missions.
 
• Statement 4, which refers to **understanding the effects on blood stem cells** during spaceflight, is valid. Such research is essential for advancing space medicine and preparing for extended missions to distant destinations like Mars.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Axiom Space:**

 
 
• Axiom Space is a private aerospace company established in **2016** and headquartered in Houston, Texas, USA.
 
• The company aims to build the world's first **commercial space station**, serving as a successor to the **International Space Station (ISS)**.
 
• Axiom missions focus on conducting research, commercial activities, and preparing for future private space stations.
 
• Previous missions, such as **Axiom‑1 and Axiom‑2**, have successfully sent private astronauts to the ISS for research and commercial endeavors.
 
 
 
• **International Space Station (ISS):**
 
 
• The ISS is a collaborative project involving five major space agencies: **NASA (USA), Roscosmos (Russia), ESA (Europe), JAXA (Japan), and CSA (Canada).**
 
• It orbits Earth at an altitude of approximately **400 km** and serves as a platform for scientific research in microgravity.
 
• Research conducted aboard the ISS includes studies in **biology, physics, astronomy, and material sciences**.
 
• It provides a unique environment to test technologies and prepare for missions to the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
 
 
 
• **Microgravity Research:**
 
 
• Microgravity refers to the condition in which objects appear to be weightless, as experienced in orbit.
 
• Research in microgravity helps scientists study phenomena that are difficult to observe under Earth's gravity, such as **fluid dynamics, combustion, and biological processes.**
 
• Key areas of study include the effects of microgravity on **human physiology**, particularly on muscles, bones, and cardiovascular health.
 
• Microgravity experiments aboard the ISS contribute to advancements in medicine, materials science, and space exploration technologies.
 
 
 
• **Space Medicine:**
 
 
• Space medicine focuses on maintaining the health and safety of astronauts during space missions.
 
• Key areas include studying the effects of **radiation, microgravity, and psychological stress** on human health.
 
• Research in space medicine is essential for the success of long-duration missions, such as those to the Moon or Mars.
 
• Findings from space medicine are also applied to improve healthcare on Earth, particularly in areas such as **telemedicine and remote diagnostics**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indian Space Station:**

 
 
• India has plans to develop its own space station by the late **2020s**, as announced by ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation).
 
• The proposed station will have a weight of **20 tons** and be capable of hosting astronauts for extended durations.
 
• Currently, India does not have operational docking capabilities for lunar bases or a space station.
 
• Testing crewed docking with a lunar base is not part of any ongoing Indian space missions.
 
 
 
• **Lunar Missions:**
 
 
• India has successfully conducted lunar missions like **Chandrayaan‑1** (2008) and **Chandrayaan‑2** (2019).
 
• The upcoming **Chandrayaan‑3** mission aims to demonstrate landing and rover capabilities on the Moon.
 
• However, these missions do not include crewed lunar bases or docking tests.
 
• Future lunar missions may focus on establishing infrastructure for human exploration of the Moon.

questions.question: The Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) lab in which city has created an advanced polymeric membrane designed for high-pressure desalination of sea water in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)**, a premier agency under the Ministry of Defence in India, developed an advanced polymeric membrane to aid in **high-pressure desalination of seawater**.
 
• This innovation was carried out by the **DRDO laboratory in Kanpur**, known for its expertise in developing advanced materials and technology solutions.
 
• The polymeric membrane developed is designed to withstand **high-pressure applications**, making it suitable for efficient desalination processes, essential for producing potable water from seawater.
 
• The technology is expected to contribute significantly to **India's efforts** in addressing water scarcity, particularly in coastal regions, by providing an affordable and sustainable solution.
 
• The development aligns with India's focus on leveraging **indigenous technology** to solve critical environmental and resource challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Defense Research and Development Organisation (DRDO):**

 
 
• Established in **1958**, DRDO works under the Ministry of Defence to develop state-of-the-art technologies for India's defense and strategic applications.
 
• It operates a network of **50 laboratories** specializing in fields like aeronautics, armaments, electronics, and advanced materials.
 
• DRDO has been instrumental in developing indigenous technologies such as the **Agni missile series, BrahMos missile system, and Tejas fighter aircraft**.
 
 
 
• **Polymeric Membranes:**
 
 
• A polymeric membrane is a synthetic material used for **separation processes**, including desalination, filtration, and purification.
 
• They are known for their **high efficiency, durability, and ability to operate in extreme pressure conditions**.
 
• Such membranes are widely used in **reverse osmosis desalination plants**, which convert saline water into potable water.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Desalination:**
 
 
• Desalination is the process of removing salts and other impurities from seawater to produce **freshwater**.
 
• It is critical for addressing **water scarcity**, especially in regions with limited freshwater resources.
 
• India has been investing in desalination technologies to cater to the needs of its growing population and industries.
 
 
 
• **Kanpur - A Hub for Advanced Research:**
 
 
• Kanpur is home to several prestigious research institutions, including the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT Kanpur)**, which contributes to innovations in technology and science.
 
• The city has emerged as a center for advancements in **material science and engineering**, making it an ideal location for a DRDO lab focused on polymeric innovations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Water Scarcity in India:**

 
 
• India is one of the most water-stressed countries in the world, with a per capita water availability of **1,544 cubic meters** as of 2020.
 
• Desalination technologies could provide a sustainable solution to meet the water demand in coastal and urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched several schemes like the **National Water Mission** and **Atal Bhujal Yojana** to manage water resources efficiently.
 
• Investments in desalination and water treatment technologies are part of India's broader strategy to ensure **water security**.

questions.question: In October 2025, which state government launched the State Climate Action Tracker alongside district-level decarbonization action plans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In **October 2025**, the **Tamil Nadu government** launched the **State Climate Action Tracker** to monitor and analyze climate-related initiatives and their impact across the state.
 
• The tracker is a part of the state’s broader efforts to achieve **decarbonization** and align with global climate goals like the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• Alongside the tracker, **district-level decarbonization action plans** were introduced to address region-specific environmental challenges and implement localized solutions.
 
• The initiative aims to strengthen Tamil Nadu’s position as a leader in **climate action** and sustainable development in India.
 
• The tracker will provide real-time data and insights into greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy adoption, and policy implementation progress at both the state and district levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tamil Nadu’s Climate Leadership:**

 
 
• Tamil Nadu is known for its proactive initiatives in renewable energy, particularly in **solar and wind power**. The state is among the top producers of renewable energy in India.
 
• The state has set ambitious targets to achieve **carbon neutrality** and reduce its reliance on fossil fuels by promoting energy efficiency and green technologies.
 
 
 
• **State Climate Action Tracker:**
 
 
• The tracker is a digital tool designed to provide comprehensive data on **emissions, energy usage**, and the implementation of climate policies.
 
• It ensures **transparency** and accountability by making climate-related information accessible to policymakers, researchers, and the public.
 
 
 
• **District-Level Decarbonization Plans:**
 
 
• These plans focus on region-specific strategies to reduce carbon emissions, such as promoting **electric vehicles**, enhancing public transport, and supporting **afforestation** programs.
 
• Local governments will play a crucial role in implementing and monitoring these plans to ensure their effectiveness.
 
 
 
• **Global Climate Goals:**
 
 
• The initiative aligns with the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly SDG 13 on climate action.
 
• It also supports India’s commitments under the **Paris Agreement**, which aims to limit global warming to below 2°C above pre-industrial levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Technology in Climate Action:**

 
 
• Advanced technologies like **artificial intelligence** and **big data analytics** are being used to monitor and predict environmental changes.
 
• These tools enhance decision-making by providing accurate and real-time data on emission trends and the effectiveness of policies.
 
 
 
• **India’s National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC):**
 
 
• Launched in **2008**, the NAPCC outlines eight missions focusing on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and sustainable agriculture, among others.
 
• State-level initiatives like Tamil Nadu’s tracker complement these national efforts by addressing local environmental challenges.
 
 
 
• **Public Participation:**
 
 
• Public awareness and participation are crucial for the success of climate action plans. Tamil Nadu aims to involve communities in activities like **tree planting** and **waste management**.
 
• Educational campaigns and workshops are being organized to promote sustainable practices among citizens.

questions.question: Which national team claimed their first-ever title at the 2025 IIHF Women’s Asia Cup?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Philippines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Philippines** claimed their first-ever title at the **2025 IIHF Women’s Asia Cup**, marking a historic milestone for their national hockey team.
 
• The victory was a significant accomplishment as the **Philippines** showcased their growing strength in ice hockey, a sport that is traditionally dominated by nations like Japan and China in Asia.
 
• Teams participating in the IIHF Women’s Asia Cup included prominent hockey nations such as **Japan, China, India**, and the **Philippines**, making the competition intense and highly competitive.
 
• The **Philippines** achieved this milestone through consistent performance, strategic gameplay, and the contribution of key players who played pivotal roles in their success.
 
• This victory reflects the nation’s commitment to developing ice hockey and fostering greater participation in winter sports despite its tropical climate and lack of natural ice surfaces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF):**

 
 
• The IIHF, founded in **1908**, is the international governing body for ice hockey and inline hockey.
 
• It organizes various tournaments, including the **IIHF World Championships, IIHF Women’s Asia Cup**, and IIHF Junior Championships.
 
• Its primary goal is to promote and develop ice hockey globally, including in regions where the sport is less popular.
 
 
 
• **Development of Ice Hockey in the Philippines:**
 
 
• Ice hockey is still a developing sport in the **Philippines**, with most ice rinks located in shopping malls due to the tropical climate.
 
• The country’s ice hockey program has been steadily growing, supported by local leagues and international exposure.
 
• In recent years, Filipino teams have participated in regional tournaments, gaining experience and improving their competitive edge.
 
 
 
• **Key Competitors in the IIHF Women’s Asia Cup:**
 
 
• **Japan:** Known for its robust hockey infrastructure and consistent performance in international tournaments.
 
• **China:** A rapidly emerging hockey powerhouse, benefiting from significant investments in winter sports ahead of events like the Winter Olympics.
 
• **India:** A developing nation in the field of ice hockey, with efforts to promote the sport in regions like Ladakh where natural ice surfaces are available.
 
• **Philippines:** Despite challenges, the nation has made remarkable progress, culminating in their first-ever title win at the **2025 IIHF Women’s Asia Cup**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of the IIHF Women’s Asia Cup:**
 
 
• The tournament plays a crucial role in promoting women’s ice hockey in Asia, encouraging greater participation and investment in the sport.
 
• It serves as a platform for emerging teams to compete at a higher level and gain international exposure.
 
• The competition fosters cultural exchange and strengthens the camaraderie among nations through sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges for Tropical Nations:**

 
 
• Countries like the **Philippines** face unique challenges in developing ice hockey due to their tropical climates and lack of natural ice.
 
• Infrastructure development, including the construction of artificial ice rinks, is crucial for the growth of the sport.
 
 
 
• **Role of International Tournaments:**
 
 
• Participating in tournaments like the IIHF Women’s Asia Cup helps emerging nations gain experience and improve their skills.
 
• Such events also inspire younger generations to take up the sport, contributing to its long-term growth.
 
 
 
• **Philippines’ Hockey Success:**
 
 
• The victory at the **2025 IIHF Women’s Asia Cup** is a testament to the dedication of players, coaches, and administrators in the Philippines.
 
• This achievement is expected to boost the popularity of ice hockey in the country and attract more resources and support for its development.

questions.question: In 2025, which Ministry of Defence initiative aimed to modernise the armed forces in cyber, AI, and integrated command?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Year of Reforms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In **2025**, the **Ministry of Defence** launched an initiative called **Year of Reforms** aimed at modernising the armed forces.
 
• This initiative focused on integrating advanced technologies such as **cybersecurity**, **artificial intelligence (AI)**, and fostering **integrated command structures**.
 
• The goal was to create a robust defence mechanism to address emerging threats such as cyber warfare and AI-driven challenges.
 
• The initiative aimed to streamline operations, enhance inter-departmental coordination, and strengthen India's defence capabilities.
 
• **Year of Reforms** served as a cornerstone for transforming traditional military strategies into tech-driven, modern defence frameworks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cybersecurity in Defence:**

 
 
• Cybersecurity has become a critical aspect of national security due to the increasing threats of cyberattacks and data breaches.
 
• The initiative aimed to strengthen India's cyber defences through dedicated programmes, advanced monitoring systems, and skilled personnel.
 
• India's focus is on protecting critical infrastructure such as military databases, missile control systems, and communication networks from cyber threats.
 
• Cybersecurity advancements include the development of **firewalls, encryption technologies, and AI-based threat detection systems**.
 
 
 
• **Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Defence:**
 
 
• AI is revolutionising military strategies with applications in **autonomous drones, predictive analytics, and threat identification**.
 
• AI enables faster decision-making and real-time analysis of battlefield data.
 
• India's defence sector is exploring AI for applications such as robotic systems, surveillance, and intelligence-gathering.
 
• AI-based systems are being deployed to enhance precision in missile systems and target tracking.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Command Structures:**
 
 
• Integrated command structures aim to unify operations across different branches of the armed forces, including the **Army, Navy, and Air Force**.
 
• This approach enhances coordination, reduces operational redundancy, and enables a more coherent defence strategy.
 
• Joint commands allow seamless sharing of resources, intelligence, and personnel during critical operations.
 
• India has been working towards establishing integrated theatre commands to address regional security challenges effectively.
 
 
 
• **Modernisation of Armed Forces:**
 
 
• Modernisation efforts include the procurement of advanced weaponry, upgrading existing systems, and adopting new technologies.
 
• India's defence budget has been increasingly allocated to research and development in cutting-edge technologies.
 
• Focus areas include **missile defence systems, space warfare capabilities, and advanced combat platforms**.
 
• Modernisation ensures that the armed forces remain prepared to counter both conventional and unconventional threats.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Digital India and Defence:** While **Digital India** is a major government programme aimed at transforming India into a digitally empowered society, its scope is broader and not specific to defence modernisation.
 
• **Make in India:** This initiative focuses on boosting indigenous manufacturing, including defence production, but does not directly address cyber, AI, or integrated command structures.
 
• **Operation Cold Start:** A military doctrine aimed at rapid mobilisation and limited warfare, but unrelated to technological modernisation in cyber and AI.
 
• **Year of Reforms:** Specifically targets modernising India's armed forces, making it the correct answer for initiatives related to cyber, AI, and integrated command.

questions.question: As of July 2025, what is the duration of the Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan released in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2021–2030**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Revised Green India Mission (GIM)**, released in **2025**, outlines an action plan for the period **2021–2030**.
 
• The mission is a part of India's commitments under the **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)** and focuses on enhancing forest cover and ecosystem services.
 
• The primary objective of the GIM is to **increase forest and tree cover** by 5 million hectares and improve the quality of another 5 million hectares of degraded forest land.
 
• The mission also emphasizes **improved ecosystem services**, including biodiversity, hydrological services, and carbon sequestration, with a focus on climate change adaptation.
 
• The **duration** of the plan aligns with India's long-term climate action goals and international commitments under the **Paris Agreement**. Hence, the timeline of **2021–2030** is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of the Green India Mission:**

 
 
• The mission aims to **restore degraded ecosystems**, including grasslands, wetlands, mangroves, and other critical habitats.
 
• It integrates **community participation**, with a focus on the involvement of women and marginalized groups in afforestation and forest management activities.
 
• Promotes the sustainable use of natural resources while ensuring the **livelihood security** of forest-dependent communities.
 
• Encourages the use of **indigenous plant species** to enhance biodiversity and resilience against climate change.
 
• Focuses on **monitoring and evaluation** through a Geographic Information System (GIS) and remote sensing technologies to track progress.
 
 
 
• **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC):**
 
 
• Launched in **2008**, NAPCC is a framework to address climate change through sustainable development.
 
• It comprises eight missions, including the Green India Mission, National Solar Mission, and National Water Mission.
 
• The focus areas include promoting **renewable energy**, enhancing energy efficiency, and ensuring water and agricultural sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement and India's Commitments:**
 
 
• India has committed to reducing its **emissions intensity** by 33–35% from 2005 levels by 2030.
 
• It aims to create an additional carbon sink of **2.5–3 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent** through forest and tree cover by 2030.
 
• The Green India Mission plays a crucial role in meeting these targets.
 
 
 
• **Global Climate Action:**
 
 
• The **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)** guides global climate policies and initiatives.
 
• India is among the leading nations advocating for **climate justice** and emphasizes the principle of **Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Importance of Forests:**

 
 
• Forests act as **carbon sinks**, absorbing CO₂ from the atmosphere and mitigating climate change.
 
• They provide critical **ecosystem services** such as water regulation, soil conservation, and biodiversity support.
 
• Forests contribute significantly to the livelihoods of **millions of people**, particularly in rural and tribal areas.
 
 
 
• **Challenges to Forest Management:**
 
 
• Deforestation and forest degradation due to **illegal logging, mining, and agricultural expansion**.
 
• Impacts of **climate change**, such as increased forest fires and shifting vegetation zones.
 
• Ensuring effective community participation and equitable benefit-sharing mechanisms.

questions.question: In February 2025, which company partnered with Roche Diagnostics for a self-sampling HPV DNA test in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Metropolis Healthcare**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, **Metropolis Healthcare**, a leading diagnostic service provider in India, partnered with **Roche Diagnostics** to introduce a self-sampling **HPV DNA test** in India.
 
• The test aims to provide an innovative and non-invasive approach to screen for **human papillomavirus (HPV)**, which is a significant cause of cervical cancer.
 
• Metropolis Healthcare's focus on advanced diagnostic solutions and Roche Diagnostics' expertise in diagnostic technologies make this collaboration a step towards enhancing women's health in India.
 
• This partnership intends to address the challenges of early detection of cervical cancer, which is a leading cause of cancer-related deaths among women in India.
 
• The self-sampling method empowers women by offering convenience, privacy, and accessibility, especially in rural and underserved areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Metropolis Healthcare:**

 
 
• Founded in **1980**, it is one of India’s leading diagnostic service providers, with a strong presence across **India and internationally**.
 
• Metropolis specializes in **clinical laboratory services, pathology, and preventive health check-ups**.
 
• It operates a network of **diagnostic centers** and offers over **4,000 tests** covering a wide range of diseases and health conditions.
 
 
 
• **Roche Diagnostics:**
 
 
• Roche Diagnostics is a division of the Swiss multinational healthcare company **Roche**.
 
• It is a global leader in in-vitro diagnostics and **cancer diagnostics**.
 
• The company is recognized for its cutting-edge diagnostic technologies, including PCR-based tests, which are pivotal in disease detection and management.
 
 
 
• **HPV DNA Test:**
 
 
• HPV (Human Papillomavirus) is a group of viruses, some of which are linked to cervical cancer.
 
• The HPV DNA test detects the genetic material of the virus, enabling early identification of women at risk.
 
• Self-sampling HPV DNA tests allow women to collect samples themselves, making the process less invasive compared to traditional Pap smears.
 
 
 
• **Cervical Cancer in India:**
 
 
• Cervical cancer is the **second most common cancer** among women in India.
 
• According to the **WHO**, India accounts for a significant proportion of the global cervical cancer burden.

questions.question: In April 2025, DRDO’s ** **Defense Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL) unit had successfully completed a long-duration ground test of an advanced scramjet combustor in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hyderabad**__.

__
 
• **DRDL (Defense Research and Development Laboratory)**, a unit under the **Defense Research and Development Organization (DRDO)**, conducted a successful long-duration ground test of an advanced scramjet combustor in **April 2025**.
 
• The test took place in **Hyderabad**, which houses one of DRDO's key facilities for advanced defense technology research and development.
 
• **Scramjet combustor technology** is pivotal for hypersonic systems, enabling efficient propulsion at speeds greater than Mach 5.
 
• Hyderabad is a central hub for defense and aerospace research in India, hosting several institutions like DRDL, RCI (Research Centre Imarat), and ASL (Advanced Systems Laboratory).
 
• The successful test signifies India’s progress in developing **indigenous hypersonic technology**, which is critical for defense applications and space exploration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scramjet Technology:**

 
 
• A **scramjet** (supersonic combustion ramjet) engine is designed for hypersonic flight, where air flows through the engine at supersonic speeds.
 
• Unlike conventional jet engines, scramjets do not have rotating components, reducing complexity and weight.
 
• Scramjets use atmospheric oxygen for combustion, eliminating the need to carry oxidizers, making them suitable for long-range applications.
 
• This technology is crucial for **hypersonic missiles**, high-speed aircraft, and **space vehicles**.
 
 
 
• **DRDO's Role:**
 
 
• The **Defense Research and Development Organization (DRDO)** is India’s premier defense R&D institution, under the Ministry of Defense.
 
• Established in **1958**, DRDO focuses on developing state-of-the-art defense systems and technologies.
 
• DRDO's achievements include **missile systems** like Agni, Prithvi, Akash, and BrahMos, as well as advanced radar, avionics, and electronic warfare systems.
 
 
 
• **Hyderabad’s Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Hyderabad is a significant center for India’s aerospace and defense industries, hosting key DRDO facilities such as **DRDL, ASL, and RCI**.
 
• It is also home to companies like Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) and Mishra Dhatu Nigam Limited (MIDHANI), which contribute to missile and material production.
 
• The city plays a critical role in India’s defense technology innovation and advancement.
 
 
 
• **Hypersonic Technology in India:**
 
 
• India is actively developing hypersonic systems, including **Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicles (HSTDV)**.
 
• DRDO successfully tested HSTDV in **2020**, marking a significant milestone in indigenous hypersonic capability.
 
• Such advancements are vital for defense applications, as hypersonic missiles can evade traditional air defense systems due to their high speed and maneuverability.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scramjet Applications:**

 
 
• Hypersonic missiles: Faster and harder to intercept, enhancing strategic deterrence.
 
• Space exploration: Scramjets can reduce launch costs by utilizing atmospheric oxygen for propulsion.
 
• High-speed aircraft: Potential to revolutionize commercial air travel with reduced flight times.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• Countries like the **USA, Russia, and China** are leading in hypersonic technology development.
 
• India’s advancements through DRDO place it among the few nations with indigenous hypersonic capabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is a state-of-the-art infrastructure, disaster-resilient facility launched by the Government of India in June 2025 for strengthening disaster preparedness and response mechanisms?

options.text: Advanced Disaster Response and Monitoring Facility

questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response (ICR-ER)** is a state-of-the-art facility launched by the **Government of India** in **June 2025** to enhance disaster preparedness and response mechanisms.
 
• This facility is designed to provide **real-time monitoring** and **centralized coordination** during disasters, ensuring efficient communication between various stakeholders.
 
• It integrates advanced technologies such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Geospatial Analysis**, and **Internet of Things (IoT)** to predict, monitor, and respond to emergencies effectively.
 
• The ICR-ER serves as a **centralized hub** for managing resources, evacuations, and relief efforts during disasters like earthquakes, floods, cyclones, and other emergencies.
 
• This initiative aligns with India's commitment to the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030)**, focusing on minimizing disaster impact through preparedness and technological advancements.
 
• It operates under the supervision of the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)**, ensuring seamless integration with national and state-level disaster management agencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Disaster Resilience in India:**

 
 
• India is prone to various natural disasters such as **earthquakes, floods, cyclones, and droughts**, impacting millions annually.
 
• The **Disaster Management Act, 2005** provides the legal framework for disaster risk reduction and response mechanisms in India.
 
• The **NDMA** oversees disaster management policies and coordinates efforts between the **central and state governments**.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response:**
 
 
• Equipped with **real-time data analytics** for early warning systems.
 
• Facilitates **inter-agency communication** and collaboration during emergencies.
 
• Includes **GIS mapping** for locating affected areas and prioritizing relief efforts.
 
• Ensures availability of **emergency response resources** such as medical supplies, evacuation plans, and shelters.
 
 
 
• **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction:**
 
 
• Adopted in **2015**, this global framework emphasizes reducing disaster risks and enhancing resilience.
 
• It focuses on **prevention, preparedness, and recovery** to mitigate the impact of disasters.
 
• India aligns its disaster management strategies with the **Sendai Framework** to ensure global best practices.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Initiatives:**
 
 
• **Centralized Crisis Management Centre:** Focuses on crisis response but lacks the advanced technological integration seen in ICR-ER.
 
• **Advanced Disaster Response and Monitoring Facility:** Primarily a monitoring initiative without centralized emergency control capabilities.
 
• **National Disaster Coordination Hub:** Coordinates disaster management efforts but does not include the real-time technological features of the ICR-ER.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Integration in Disaster Management:**

 
 
• Technologies like **AI** and **IoT** enable predictive analysis and proactive measures during disasters.
 
• Use of **satellite imagery** and **drones** enhances surveillance and resource allocation.
 
• Advanced communication systems ensure uninterrupted connectivity during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Global Examples of Emergency Response Systems:**
 
 
• The United States operates the **Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA)** for disaster response and recovery.
 
• Japan's **Disaster Medical Assistance Teams (DMATs)** focus on medical relief during emergencies.
 
• India's ICR-ER is among the few global initiatives integrating advanced technologies for disaster resilience.

questions.question: The Andhra Pradesh government rejected Telangana's demand for a 50 : 50 share of Krishna river water in January 2025. Currently, what is the water sharing ratio between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**66 : 34**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Current Water Sharing Ratio:** The water sharing ratio between **Andhra Pradesh** and **Telangana** is **66 : 34**. Andhra Pradesh receives 66% of the Krishna river water allocation, while Telangana receives the remaining 34%.
 
• **Demand Rejected:** In **January 2025**, the Andhra Pradesh government rejected Telangana's demand for a **50 : 50** share of Krishna river water.
 
• **Reorganization Context:** The current water-sharing arrangement was established after the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh and the creation of Telangana in **2014**. The allocation was based on various factors, including existing irrigation projects, population, and geographical requirements.
 
• **Krishna River Details:** The Krishna River is one of the major rivers in India, flowing through the states of **Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana**. It is crucial for irrigation, drinking water, and hydropower generation in these regions.
 
• **Disputes:** Water-sharing disputes between states in India are common due to varying demands for irrigation, industrial use, and drinking water. The Krishna River water-sharing dispute is managed by the **Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal (KWDT)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal (KWDT):**

 
 
• The KWDT was established under the **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956**. Its purpose is to resolve disputes related to the Krishna River water-sharing among states.
 
• The tribunal has issued multiple awards (KWDT-I in **1976** and KWDT-II in **2010**) to allocate water among the basin states.
 
• The KWDT-II award allocated water based on 65% dependability, taking into consideration the needs of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, and Maharashtra.
 
 
 
• **Krishna River Basin:**
 
 
• The Krishna River originates near **Mahabaleshwar** in Maharashtra and flows through Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The basin area spans approximately **258,948 square kilometers**, covering around 8% of India's total geographical area.
 
• Major tributaries include the **Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi, and Koyna**.
 
 
 
• **Water Allocation Principles:**
 
 
• Water allocation among states is based on factors such as existing infrastructure, geographical area, population, and water availability.
 
• States often negotiate or approach tribunals for equitable water-sharing based on their irrigation and drinking water needs.
 
 
 
• **Inter-State Disputes in India:**
 
 
• Inter-state river disputes are governed by the **Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956**.
 
• Notable disputes include the **Cauvery Water Dispute** (Karnataka-Tamil Nadu), **Godavari Water Dispute**, and the **Ravi-Beas Dispute**.
 
• These disputes highlight the challenges in equitable water distribution across states with varying needs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Andhra Pradesh-Telangana Bifurcation:**

 
 
• The Andhra Pradesh Reorganization Act, **2014**, led to the creation of Telangana as India's 29th state.
 
• Post-bifurcation, water resources were divided based on existing usage and infrastructure.
 
• Telangana's demand for equal sharing arises from its need for equitable access to river water for irrigation and drinking water.
 
 
 
• **Water Scarcity Concerns:**
 
 
• India faces increasing challenges related to water scarcity due to **population growth, climate change, and over-extraction**.
 
• Efficient water management and resolution of disputes are crucial for sustainable development.
 
• International examples, like the **Mekong River Commission**, offer insights into collaborative water-sharing mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Water Usage:**
 
 
• States are encouraged to adopt efficient irrigation techniques such as **drip irrigation** and rainwater harvesting.
 
• Promoting inter-state cooperation and adherence to tribunal awards can help resolve disputes amicably.

questions.question: International Labour Day 2025 was celebrated globally on which of the following dates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fri May 01 2026 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International Labour Day**, also known as **May Day**, is celebrated annually on **May 1st** across the globe to honor the contributions of workers and the labor movement.
 
• The first May Day was celebrated in **1889** after the establishment of the International Socialist Congress in Paris to commemorate the **Haymarket affair of 1886**.
 
• **Fri May 01 2026** is the accurate date for International Labour Day in 2026 as it aligns with the annual observation of the day on **May 1st**.
 
• International Labour Day symbolizes the struggle for **fair labor practices, rights, and better working conditions** for workers worldwide.
 
• It is recognized as a public holiday in many countries, including **India**, where workers participate in various events such as rallies, marches, and discussions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of International Labour Day:**

 
 
• International Labour Day originated from the labor union movement advocating for an **eight-hour workday**.
 
• The **Haymarket affair**, a major labor protest in Chicago in **1886**, played a pivotal role in establishing May 1st as Labour Day.
 
• The day became internationally recognized after the **Second International** declared May 1st as International Workers' Day in **1889**.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• Labour Day serves as a reminder of the **struggles and achievements** of workers over the years.
 
• It highlights the importance of ensuring **fair wages, safe working conditions, and social protections**.
 
• It is a day to express solidarity with workers globally and promote **economic equality**.
 
 
 
• **Observance in India:**
 
 
• Labour Day was first celebrated in **India** on **May 1, 1923**, in **Chennai** by the **Labour Kisan Party of Hindustan**.
 
• It is a public holiday in several states, with workers' unions organizing rallies, speeches, and cultural events.
 
• The day is an opportunity to acknowledge the vital contributions of workers in India's economic progress.
 
 
 
• **Global Observance:**
 
 
• Many countries, including the **United States, United Kingdom, and Australia**, observe Labour Day but on different dates due to historical and cultural differences.
 
• In some countries, such as **China, Russia, and Germany**, May Day is a significant national holiday with parades and celebrations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Haymarket Affair:**

 
 
• The **Haymarket Affair** was a labor protest in Chicago in **May 1886** that turned violent, leading to several deaths and inspiring the global labor movement.
 
• It emphasized the need for **workers' rights** and became the cornerstone for observing May Day.
 
 
 
• **International Labour Organization (ILO):**
 
 
• The ILO, established in **1919**, plays a crucial role in promoting **global labor standards**.
 
• It advocates for **decent work conditions, fair wages, and employment opportunities** worldwide.
 
• ILO conventions and recommendations guide nations in improving labor practices.
 
 
 
• **Modern-day Observance:**
 
 
• Labour Day is marked by **rallies, speeches, and demonstrations** to address labor-related issues.
 
• It serves as a platform for workers to voice their concerns regarding **employment, wages, and workplace safety**.
 
• Educational institutions and organizations use the day to raise awareness about the **rights and responsibilities** of workers.

questions.question: Which renowned personality received the 2025 Templeton Prize for promoting science and spirituality?

The correct answer is __**Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew**, a global leader of the Orthodox Christian Church, is recognized for his contributions towards promoting **science and spirituality**.
 
• He was awarded the **2025 Templeton Prize**, which honors individuals whose work has advanced the intersection of science and religion.
 
• Patriarch Bartholomew has been an advocate for **environmental sustainability**, often referred to as the "Green Patriarch" for his efforts in connecting ecology with theology.
 
• His initiatives emphasize the need for **spiritual reflection** on environmental issues, urging global communities to adopt sustainable practices.
 
• The Templeton Prize, established by Sir John Templeton, is one of the world's largest annual awards in monetary terms, celebrating work that bridges gaps between **science, philosophy, and religion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew:**

 
 
• He is the **Archbishop of Constantinople-New Rome** and Ecumenical Patriarch, serving as the spiritual leader of approximately 300 million Orthodox Christians worldwide.
 
• He has played a significant role in fostering interfaith dialogue and promoting **peaceful coexistence** among different religious groups.
 
• His efforts include organizing environmental conferences and advocating for **climate justice**.
 
• Bartholomew has consistently highlighted the moral and spiritual dimensions of environmental degradation.
 
 
 
• **Templeton Prize:**
 
 
• Established in **1972** by Sir John Templeton, the award recognizes individuals making exceptional contributions to affirming life's spiritual dimension.
 
• It is awarded annually and includes a monetary value higher than the Nobel Prizes to reflect Sir Templeton's belief in the importance of spiritual contributions.
 
• Past recipients include influential figures like **Mother Teresa**, **Dalai Lama**, and **Francis Collins**.
 
 
 
• **Intersection of Science and Spirituality:**
